paragraphs: The following assessments concern how mathematicians research and model. They do not predict hiring, qualifications, authorization, or research results.

Mathematicians focus on advancing mathematics and applying it to practical problems: researching traditional fields such as algebra, geometry, probability, and logic to expand mathematical knowledge; developing new principles and relationships among existing principles; formulating hypotheses and deriving their consequences; conducting numerical analysis and computation; building mathematical models for analysis or computational simulation; applying mathematical theory and techniques to practical problems in business, engineering, science, and other fields; developing computational solution methods; communicating findings through reports, papers, and conferences; and instructing others in mathematical methods.

Entirely fictional task package: Provide a fictional problem context and data, including 1 problem description with constraints, 1 set of available observations or simulation data, and 1 modeling or proof objective. Within 60 minutes, write modeling assumptions and a mathematical formulation, a solution or proof approach, verification methods and limitations, and explain how the results can be tested. Do not use real confidential data or others' unpublished findings.

Sample output and reflection: Check whether you first defined the problem and assumptions, explained methods and applicability conditions, provided verifiable conclusions and limitations, and clearly distinguished proof from numerical approximation. Then ask whether you can sustain derivation and computation, persist through long periods without results while honestly acknowledging uncertainty, and take responsibility for conclusions and citation standards.

Mathematicians on this page refers to O*NET 15-2021.00: professionals who research fundamental mathematics or applications of mathematical techniques to science, management, and other fields and solve problems using mathematical methods. Titles include computational mathematician and cryptography researcher. Work includes fundamental mathematics research, developing new relationships among mathematical principles, formulating hypotheses and deriving consequences, numerical analysis and computation, mathematical modeling for analysis or simulation, applying mathematical techniques to business, engineering, and scientific problems, developing computational methods, writing papers and reports, giving academic presentations, and instructing others in mathematical methods. Work is mainly in offices and computing environments. This page excludes adjacent roles such as financial quantitative analysts, computer and information research scientists, operations research analysts, statisticians, and biostatisticians.

entries: Work inputs: Mathematical problems and conjectures, observational or simulated data, assumptions and axiomatic conditions, computational and numerical methods, modeling needs and application contexts, literature and existing findings, and funding and collaboration information.

Verifiable outputs: Proofs and theorems, models and mathematical formulations, numerical calculations and simulation results, algorithms and computational methods, research reports and papers, academic presentations and handouts, and conclusions and recommendations for applied problems.

Complete workflow: Define the problem and assumptions → review literature and select methods → derive or model and compute → verify results and boundaries → document and present findings → undergo review and revise to complete the cycle.

paragraphs: Work reality: O*NET 15-2021.00 respondents report mainly indoor work with written and team communication. Research requires sustained derivation, computation, and review; verify working hours by institution and project. Key judgments concern clarity of problems and assumptions, method and model applicability, sufficient proof or verification, controllable numerical error, and compliance with citation and research output boundaries.

Environment and pace: Mainly controlled indoor and computing environments, with communication through documents and meetings, high decision-making freedom, emphasis on precision, and strong competition. Most work more than 40 hours a week and spend long periods on derivation and computation.

Research inputs: Occupational identity, tasks, work activities, work context, skills and knowledge, interest code, education, and Job Zone for O*NET 15-2021.00. Wage, employment, and industry data on that page cover this occupation. Research findings are not used to infer mainland Chinese qualifications, pay, or employment definitions.

Check first: Problems and assumptions, method and model applicability conditions, data and computation definitions, verification and error requirements, academic standards and funding boundaries, and the scope of applications.

Work cycle: Start by defining problems and assumptions, then review literature and select methods, derive or model and compute, verify results, document findings, and undergo review. Do not draw conclusions before confirming all assumptions and method applicability conditions, or submit for publication before checking citations and output boundaries.

Boundaries with adjacent roles: This page covers only mathematicians. Financial quantitative analysts focus on financial modeling and trading; computer and information research scientists on computing and information research; operations research analysts on optimization; statisticians and biostatisticians on statistical inference and biomedical data. Their objects and methods are not interchangeable with those on this page.
Financial quantitative analysts focus on financial market models and trading strategies; mathematicians focus on mathematical theory and applied research, with different objectives and deliverables.

Computer and information research scientists focus on frontier computing and information science research; mathematicians focus on mathematical theory and applications, with different methodological emphases.
Operations research analysts focus on resource and decision optimization; mathematicians focus on mathematical theory and broader applications, with different sources of problems.

Statisticians and biostatisticians focus on data inference and biomedical applications; mathematicians focus on mathematical theory and applications in other fields, with different objectives and verification methods.
Boundaries of AI impact on mathematicians

Tools for symbolic computation and theorem-proving assistance, numerical computation and optimization, literature and data searches, and paper and handout drafting can assist with calculation verification, idea exploration, and material organization. Researchers remain responsible for problem definition, assumption selection, proof and modeling judgments, conclusion reliability, and academic standards. Tools must not replace rigorous reasoning and review.

Occupational sources describe actual tasks and objects of work: problems and assumptions, models and proofs, computation and data, and papers and reports. Tool capabilities, institutional adoption, and job outcomes are recorded separately. Wage or employment data are not substitutes for AI evidence.

Editorial analysis: Try tools for symbolic computation, numerical experiments, and drafting, comparing accuracy, verifiability, and cost for each. Existing occupational task and exposure research cannot establish which stage will see adoption first or greater employment impact.

Human control points: Define problems and assumptions, judge method and model applicability, verify conclusions and errors, take responsibility for findings and citation standards, and follow academic ethics and funding agreements.

First conduct an offline exercise with an entirely fictional problem context and data. Write modeling assumptions, a solution or proof approach, and verification methods without relying on unverified automated computation or proofs to replace rigorous reasoning.
Editorial recommendation: Tools may assist symbolic computation, numerical experiments, and drafting. Current materials do not demonstrate widespread institutional adoption of these systems.
Follow assumptions, method applicability, and academic standards, retaining human judgment and records.

U.S. pay and employment scope for mathematicians (occupation 15-2021.00)

U.S. national mathematicians (15-2021): BLS 2025 median annual wage of $126,710, with the 10th percentile at $69,240 and the 90th at $195,190. These are not starting pay or seniority levels. O*NET currently displays about 2,200 employed in 2025, 1%–2% growth in 2025–2035, and about 100 average annual openings. The overall projection is not attributed to AI and does not equal current job postings or individual opportunities.

BLS 2025 wages listed separately for mathematicians: The median and 10th and 90th percentiles describe the national wage distribution, not minimum or maximum wages, seniority levels, or take-home income.

Percentiles are not seniority: About 10% of wages are below the 10th percentile and about 10% above the 90th. Institutions, regions, and tasks differ; beginner or senior income cannot be inferred from percentiles.

Major employers of mathematicians in 2025 include the federal government and educational institutions. The table below uses specific industry median annual wages from the mathematician subtable in BLS Pay, separately from industry employment shares.

The current outlook uses 2025–2035 projections: About 2,200 mathematicians employed, an O*NET growth category of 1%–2%, and about 100 average annual openings. Do not mix this with the combined mathematician and statistician group. The projection is not attributed to AI.
Fit signals: Start with observable work behaviors

To assess fit, consider whether you can sustain abstract derivation and computation, reason rigorously and treat uncertainty honestly, model practical problems mathematically, read literature and write, and continue producing work in a competitive environment. Tools such as RIASEC only generate hypotheses and cannot replace actual task experience.
Positive signals: Abstract thinking and rigorous reasoning, sustained focus, mathematical modeling of practical problems, honesty about uncertainty, and continued reading and writing.

Reasons for caution: Difficulty sustaining abstract derivation, a tendency to skip verification or overstate conclusions, unwillingness to write and undergo review, or difficulty handling competition and long periods without results.

Trial action: With an entirely fictional problem context and data, practice developing modeling assumptions, a solution approach, and verification methods, then ask someone to review them against your records.

The O*NET interest code is IC (Investigative–Conventional): an inclination toward research and analysis and organizing symbolic information according to procedures. These labels describe activity preferences only and cannot determine competence or qualifications.

General personality measures such as the Big Five provide no job-specific evidence for this occupation and support self-reflection only. Continue checking through actual derivation and proof, modeling and computation, and writing and presentation experience.
Type tools such as MBTI and the Enneagram cannot determine competence or qualifications and support self-reflection only.

Entry pathways and capability stages

In the U.S., this occupation is in Job Zone 5 (extensive preparation needed). Most positions require graduate education; respondents report about 45% doctorates, 25% master's degrees, and 10% bachelor's degrees. Extensive related experience is usually needed. Verify specific requirements with institutions and employers.

U.S.: BLS states that mathematics or statistics typically requires a master's degree or higher, with some positions accepting bachelor's degrees. Doctorates may lead toward university research and teaching; read institutional notices for appointment requirements. Insufficient evidence: Matching authority materials on a uniform qualification system for mathematician positions in mainland China were not obtained. A U.S. occupational code cannot establish the absence of requirements. Check research appointments, titles, projects, and funding with the specific institution.

Degrees, positions, and review eligibility are different statuses. Completing a degree or obtaining certification does not automatically confer a position or title. Check title evaluation and project and funding application conclusions against responsible authority and institutional rules.

Entry stage: Under supervision, practice literature reading and problem definition, basic derivation and numerical computation, modeling and programming, academic writing, and presentations. Learn academic standards and retain process records.

Evidence to show: Use a verifiable research or modeling explanation, including problem and assumptions, methods and calculations, conclusions and limitations, to demonstrate rigorous reasoning and honest documentation.

Next step: Check the target institution's research direction and requirements, findings and citation standards, and project and funding conditions. Verify modeling, computation, and writing skills in supervised real research.

Progression to greater responsibility: With experience, lead independent projects and directions, mentor and collaborate in teams, develop a specialty, or move into applied research, data analysis, or teaching.

Transferable capabilities: Abstract reasoning and proof, mathematical modeling and numerical computation, programming and algorithms, data analysis, academic writing and presentations, cross-disciplinary applications, and collaboration.

Gaps to address: Applied knowledge and programming skills in the target field, statistics and machine learning methods, or experience and evidence of responsibility for transitions into operations optimization, data science, and quantitative analysis.

description.text: Mathematicians on this page refers to O*NET 15-2021.00: conducting fundamental mathematics research, developing new relationships among mathematical principles, formulating hypotheses and deriving consequences, conducting numerical analysis and computation, developing mathematical models for analysis or simulation, applying mathematical techniques to business, engineering, and scientific problems, writing papers, and giving academic presentations. To assess this career path, verify the work cycle, responsibility and evidence boundaries, evidence definitions, risk controls, and observable entry-level work samples together.

subject.summary: Mathematicians on this page refers to O*NET 15-2021.00: professionals researching fundamental mathematics or applications of mathematical techniques to science, management, and other fields and solving problems using mathematical methods. Titles include computational mathematician and cryptography researcher.
